- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.3) mid-period, adjust forecast downward by 3–8% to reflect risk aversion.  
- For 30-day horizons, if recent 5-day average is rising and sentiment is neutral or positive, expect mean reversion within 10–15 days — reduce forecast slope slightly.  
- If forecast spikes after a strong positive sentiment surge, cap the peak at 1.5x the 14-day moving average to prevent overreaction.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating ±0.5), use 10-day weighted average of history to smooth forecast, avoiding overfitting to short-term sentiment.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below forecast, apply a 2–3% downward bias to correct for overconfidence in upward momentum.
